Article 4

Letter a
What is meant by trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification of documents or identity, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control or that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

Letter b
What is meant by exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical sexual reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring/utilizing labor or transplanting organs and or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.

Letter c
Sufficiently clear.

Letter d
Sufficiently clear.

Letter e
What is meant by witness is a person who sees, hears and experiences events of violence and human rights violations.

Letter f
Mediation is carried out for cases of domestic violence that fall into the category of complaint offenses as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence.

Article 27

1. The domestic violence prevention group at the village/sub-district level as referred to in Article 23 letter d, is a functional work unit that provides integrated protection services and handling of cases of violence against women and children at the village/sub-district level.
2. The domestic violence prevention group at the village/sub-district level as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements of village/sub-district officials, elements of babinsa and elements of babinkamtibmas, community leaders/religious leaders, and youth elements.
3. Further provisions regarding the establishment, duties and functions of the task force as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by village head/sub-district head decree.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Belitung Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Belitung.
4. Regional Apparatus Organization, hereinafter abbreviated as OPD, is the Regional Apparatus of Belitung Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of Belitung Regency.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, or psychological to the victim.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and/or for and on behalf of another party who is their dependent.
10. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
11. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing, or having occurred violence against victims.
13. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
14. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Accompaniment is activities and actions carried out by companions to women and children.
16. Counseling is the provision of assistance by a person who is expert/trained in such a way that the psychological understanding and ability of the victim and/or perpetrator increases in solving the problems faced.
17. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
18. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for the prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is established at the regency, sub-district and village/kelurahan levels.
19. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
21. Household is family members and relatives including grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and non-relatives including domestic helpers and drivers who live and eat from 1 (one) kitchen and reside in 1 (one) house.

Article 10

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 8 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence. (3) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 5

Letter a
Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
Sexual violence is caused by:
1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d
Neglect is caused by:
1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of a child as they should, carried out by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they must provide life, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e
Coercion/Deprivation of Freedom is a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will and restricts their freedom as a human being who has the right to determine choices.

Letter f
Exploitation is caused by:
1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
2. acts with or without the consent of the victim including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter g
Threat of certain actions is a form of intimidation to do or not do what is requested by the perpetrator with consequences that are not good for the victim.

Letter h
Other violence is caused among others by any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear.

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so on.

Therefore....

D:\PERDA PDF\2-PERDA PERLINDUNGAN HAK PEREMPUAN DAN ANAK.doc 21 Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of the Rights of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of the Rights of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government and the participation of the business sector and community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be eliminated. Through this Regional Regulation it is hoped that the rights of children and women and their protection can be better implemented, so that it can be implemented more comprehensively, integrated and continuously by government elements, families and the community as well as other institutions related to child and women protection efforts.

Article 29

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of acts of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of acts of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who are withdrawn/neglected from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 31

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the provision of protection for women and children from acts of violence.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2), is in order to realize the objectives of protecting the rights of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by relevant OPD/agencies and the community.

Article 26

1. The task force for the protection of women and children at the sub-district level as referred to in Article 23 letter c, is a functional work unit that provides integrated protection services and handling of cases of violence against women and children at the sub-district level.
2. The membership of the task force for the protection of women and children at the sub-district level as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements of sub-district officials, agencies/institutions at the sub-district level, elements of the sector police (Polsek), elements of the military rayon command (Koramil), community leaders/religious leaders, and youth elements.
3. Further provisions regarding the establishment, duties and functions of the task force as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by Sub-district Head Decree.

Article 11

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 8 letter c and letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 18

The Regional Government is obliged to provide complaint services for the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

CHAPTER X

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 22

1. In the context of providing protection services to women and children from acts of violence, the Regional Government establishes PPT as an integrated service center in the protection of women and children from acts of violence including victims of violence.
2. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), functions as an integrated service center in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.
3. Further provisions regarding the Organization and Work Procedures of PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 31

Paragraph (1)
What is meant by guidance on the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence is efforts made by the Regional Government and the Community to realize the achievement of the objectives of prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence.

What is meant by supervision of the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence is a process of activities aimed at ensuring that efforts made by the Regional Government and the Community run efficiently and effectively in accordance with plans and provisions of laws and regulations.

Paragraph (2)
Sufficiently clear.

Sufficiently clear.

Article 17

Paragraph (1)
Letter a
What is meant by complaint services is a series of actions taken by the organizers of integrated service institutions to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families and/or the community.

Letter b
What is meant by health services is efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.

Letter c
What is meant by legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.

Letter d
What is meant by social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.

What is meant by social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

Letter e
What is meant by repatriation is returning women and child victims of violence from Belitung Regency or from the receiving area to the area of origin.

Letter f
What is meant by identification services is services to determine the background of problems and identification of victims.

Letter g
What is meant by psychological services is services to restore the mental and psychological condition of victims to return to normal.

Paragraph (2)
Sufficiently Clear.

Paragraph (3)
What is meant by minimum service standards (SPM) is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and child victims of violence.

Paragraph (4)
Sufficiently Clear.

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so on.

Therefore....

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of the Rights of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government and the participation of the business sector and community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be eliminated. Through this Regional Regulation it is hoped that the rights of children and women and their protection can be better implemented, so that it can be implemented more comprehensively, integrated and continuously by government elements, families and the community as well as other institutions related to child and women protection efforts.

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so on.

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so on.

Therefore....

D:\PERDA PDF\2-PERDA PERLINDUNGAN HAK PEREMPUAN DAN ANAK.doc 21 Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of the Rights of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of the Rights of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government and the participation of the business sector and community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be eliminated. Through this Regional Regulation it is hoped that the rights of children and women and their protection can be better implemented, so that it can be implemented more comprehensively, integrated and continuously by government elements, families and the community as well as other institutions related to child and women protection efforts.

3. Further provisions regarding the establishment, duties and functions of the task force as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by Sub-district Head Decree.

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so on.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, or psychological to the victim.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and/or for and on behalf of another party who is their dependent.

14. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Accompaniment is activities and actions carried out by companions to women and children.

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so on.

Therefore....

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of the Rights of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government and the participation of the business sector and community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be eliminated. Through this Regional Regulation it is hoped that the rights of children and women and their protection can be better implemented, so that it can be implemented more comprehensively, integrated and continuously by government elements, families and the community as well as other institutions related to child and women protection efforts.

c. performance.
3. Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented at least once every 3 (three) months.

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so on.

Therefore....

2. forced sexual intercourse;

1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so on.

Therefore....

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of the Rights of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government and the participation of the business sector and community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be eliminated. Through this Regional Regulation it is hoped that the rights of children and women and their protection can be better implemented, so that it can be implemented more comprehensively, integrated and continuously by government elements, families and the community as well as other institutions related to child and women protection efforts.

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so on.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Belitung Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Belitung.

8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, or psychological to the victim.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and/or for and on behalf of another party who is their dependent.

Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for the prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is established at the regency, sub-district and village/kelurahan levels.

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so on.

Therefore....

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of the Rights of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government and the participation of the business sector and community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be eliminated. Through this Regional Regulation it is hoped that the rights of children and women and their protection can be better implemented, so that it can be implemented more comprehensively, integrated and continuously by government elements, families and the community as well as other institutions related to child and women protection efforts.

3. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter h

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so on.

Therefore....

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of the Rights of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government and the participation of the business sector and community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be eliminated. Through this Regional Regulation it is hoped that the rights of children and women and their protection can be better implemented, so that it can be implemented more comprehensively, integrated and continuously by government elements, families and the community as well as other institutions related to child and women protection efforts.

Letter a

Letter b
Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
Sexual violence is caused by:
1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d
Neglect is caused by:
1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of a child as they should, carried out by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they must provide life, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e
Coercion/Deprivation of Freedom is a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will and restricts their freedom as a human being who has the right to determine choices.

Letter f
Exploitation is caused by:
1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
2. acts with or without the consent of the victim including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter g
Threat of certain actions is a form of intimidation to do or not do what is requested by the perpetrator with consequences that are not good for the victim.

Letter h
Other violence is caused among others by any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear.

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so on.

Therefore....

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of the Rights of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government and the participation of the business sector and community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be eliminated. Through this Regional Regulation it is hoped that the rights of children and women and their protection can be better implemented, so that it can be implemented more comprehensively, integrated and continuously by government elements, families and the community as well as other institutions related to child and women protection efforts.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Belitung Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Belitung.
4. Regional Apparatus Organization, hereinafter abbreviated as OPD, is the Regional Apparatus of Belitung Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of Belitung Regency.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, or psychological to the victim.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and/or for and on behalf of another party who is their dependent.
10. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
11. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing, or having occurred violence against victims.
13. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
14. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Accompaniment is activities and actions carried out by companions to women and children.
16. Counseling is the provision of assistance by a person who is expert/trained in such a way that the psychological understanding and ability of the victim and/or perpetrator increases in solving the problems faced.
17. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
18. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for the prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is established at the regency, sub-district and village/kelurahan levels.
19. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
21. Household is family members and relatives including grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and non-relatives including domestic helpers and drivers who live and eat from 1 (one) kitchen and reside in 1 (one) house.

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so on.

Therefore....

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of the Rights of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government and the participation of the business sector and community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be eliminated. Through this Regional Regulation it is hoped that the rights of children and women and their protection can be better implemented, so that it can be implemented more comprehensively, integrated and continuously by government elements, families and the community as well as other institutions related to child and women protection efforts.

Letter a
Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
Sexual violence is caused by:
1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d
Neglect is caused by:
1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of a child as they should, carried out by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they must provide life, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e
Coercion/Deprivation of Freedom is a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will and restricts their freedom as a human being who has the right to determine choices.

Letter f
Exploitation is caused by:
1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
2. acts with or without the consent of the victim including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter g
Threat of certain actions is a form of intimidation to do or not do what is requested by the perpetrator with consequences that are not good for the victim.

Letter h
Other violence is caused among others by any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear.

Article 8

a. regional government;
b. community;
c. family; and

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so on.

In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government and the participation of the business sector and community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be eliminated. Through this Regional Regulation it is hoped that the rights of children and women and their protection can be better implemented, so that it can be implemented more comprehensively, integrated and continuously by government elements, families and the community as well as other institutions related to child and women protection efforts.

Article 5

Letter a
Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
Sexual violence is caused by:
1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d
Neglect is caused by:
1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of a child as they should, carried out by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they must provide life, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e
Coercion/Deprivation of Freedom is a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will and restricts their freedom as a human being who has the right to determine choices.

Letter f
Exploitation is caused by:
1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
2. acts with or without the consent of the victim including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter g
Threat of certain actions is a form of intimidation to do or not do what is requested by the perpetrator with consequences that are not good for the victim.

Letter h
Other violence is caused among others by any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear.
